summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 32.0.

prs.description: doc: recommend script_flags instead of deployments.taproot
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR updates Bitcoin Core documentation to recommend using `script_flags` for validating Taproot scripts. This simplifies configuration for users and ensures better compatibility with future consensus rule changes.
prs.technical_summary: The change advises against the specific `deployments.taproot` flag in favor of the more general `script_flags` mechanism. This involves revising documentation examples and explanatory text to reflect the preferred approach for enabling script validation features. This clarifies the distinction between consensus deployment flags and runtime script validation flags, improving user guidance for advanced script usage.

prs.description: mempool: asynchronous mempool fee rate diagram updates via validation interface
prs.author: ismaelsadeeq
prs.public_summary: This enhancement improves the responsiveness of Bitcoin Core's mempool statistics by allowing fee rate diagrams to update without interrupting other critical operations. It provides users with smoother access to real-time mempool data.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces an asynchronous mechanism for updating mempool fee rate diagrams. Instead of direct, synchronous calls, the updates are now triggered via the `ValidationInterface`, leveraging its observer pattern. This design decouples the diagram generation from the main validation and mempool processing threads, preventing potential blocking. Workers listening to the `ValidationInterface` events can then process and update the diagram data in a non-blocking fashion, improving overall application responsiveness and UI fluidity.

prs.description: guix: update time-machine to c5eee3336cc1d10a3cc1c97fde2809c3451624d3
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the build environment used by Bitcoin Core for deterministic builds. This ensures our software is built with the latest compatible Guix definitions, contributing to the security and reproducibility of official releases.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request updates the `time-machine` commit hash within the Guix build descriptors to `c5eee3336cc1d10a3cc1c97fde2809c3451624d3`. This action pins the Guix environment to a newer revision, ensuring that the Guix packages and channels used for Bitcoin Core's deterministic builds are updated. This helps maintain a robust and reproducible build process by incorporating bug fixes or improvements from the Guix ecosystem without altering the Bitcoin Core application code itself.

prs.description: tor: limit torcontrol line size that is processed to prevent OOM
prs.author: davidgumberg
prs.public_summary: This PR limits the maximum line size processed from the Tor control port, preventing potential out-of-memory (OOM) issues. This enhances the node's resilience and security against malicious Tor proxies.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request introduces a critical resource management and security improvement for Bitcoin Core's interaction with the Tor control port. It implements a maximum line length check when reading incoming data from the Tor proxy. Any line exceeding this predefined limit will be truncated or result in an error, effectively preventing the client from allocating arbitrarily large memory buffers for excessively long or malformed input. This mitigation protects against denial-of-service vectors where a compromised Tor proxy could attempt to trigger OOM conditions or buffer overflows.

prs.description: rpc, mempool: -deprecatedrpc fullrbf and bip125-replaceable from mempool RPCs
prs.author: rkrux
prs.public_summary: This PR deprecates and prepares for the removal of the `fullrbf` and `bip125-replaceable` parameters from mempool-related RPC commands. This streamlines the RPC interface by eliminating redundant or outdated options, simplifying interactions for developers and focusing on core transaction replacement behavior.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation involves modifying the RPC command definitions for affected mempool queries, such as `getmempoolentry` and `getrawmempool`. The `-deprecatedrpc` flag is applied to these parameters, meaning they will still be accepted for a grace period but will trigger a warning, signaling their eventual removal in a future release. These parameters became redundant as the `mempoolfullrbf` configuration option became the primary control for full RBF behavior, making specific RPC flags for individual transactions less necessary and potentially confusing. The core change is in the parsing and validation logic of the affected RPCs to reflect this deprecation.

prs.description: indexes: Don't commit ahead of the flushed chainstate
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the robustness of Bitcoin Core's data indexing by ensuring that indexes only commit data for blocks that have been fully processed and saved by the main chainstate. This prevents potential data inconsistencies and enhances the reliability of the node's indexed information.
prs.technical_summary: This change introduces a synchronization mechanism to prevent indexes (e.g., txindex, blockfilterindex) from committing their state for a block until the corresponding chainstate flush has completed and persisted for that block. Previously, an index might attempt to persist its state for a block before the `CChainState` had fully written that block's data to disk, leading to potential data divergence upon a crash or restart. The fix likely involves coordinating commit points, perhaps by waiting for a signal or using a shared state that confirms the chainstate's persistence for a given block before an index is allowed to commit its own state.

prs.description: rpc: Disallow captures in RPCMethodImpl
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the security and maintainability of Bitcoin Core's RPC system by preventing the use of lambda captures within `RPCMethodImpl`. This enforces clearer ownership semantics and reduces potential for unexpected behavior or memory issues.
prs.technical_summary: `RPCMethodImpl` is a macro or template used to define RPC methods. Lambda captures can introduce subtle bugs related to object lifetimes and concurrency in a multi-threaded server environment. This change likely modifies the `RPCMethodImpl` definition or introduces static analysis checks to detect and disallow lambda functions that capture variables from their surrounding scope, encouraging a more explicit and safer passing of parameters for RPC method implementations.

prs.description: cmake: Get rid of undocumented `BITCOIN_GENBUILD_NO_GIT` environment variable
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR simplifies Bitcoin Core's build system by removing an obscure and undocumented environment variable, making the compilation process cleaner and easier to manage.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes the `BITCOIN_GENBUILD_NO_GIT` environment variable from the CMake build configuration. This variable was undocumented and provided an alternative method to bypass Git information during build generation, which is no longer deemed necessary or beneficial. Removing it streamlines the build system, reduces maintenance overhead, and ensures a more consistent build process.

prs.description: rpc: fix initialization-order-fiasco by lazy-init of decodepsbt_inputs
prs.author: Crypt-iQ
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a subtle bug in the `decodepsbt_inputs` RPC, preventing potential crashes or unexpected behavior due to incorrect initialization. It improves the reliability and stability of a core RPC function within Bitcoin Core.
prs.technical_summary: The issue was an initialization-order fiasco where certain RPC data structures were accessed before full construction. This PR resolves it by implementing lazy initialization for dependencies of `decodepsbt_inputs`. Components are now initialized on first use rather than through static or early global means, ensuring all necessary resources are ready when the function is called and preventing uninitialized memory access.

prs.description: validation: correct lifetime of precomputed tx data
prs.author: darosior
prs.public_summary: This PR corrects a subtle issue related to the memory management of precomputed transaction data during validation. It ensures data lifetimes are handled properly, enhancing the stability and reliability of the validation engine.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses a bug in the transaction validation subsystem concerning the lifetime of precomputed data, such as script caches or signature hashes. It specifically fixes scenarios where such data might be prematurely deallocated or accessed after being freed, potentially leading to use-after-free vulnerabilities or crashes. The change involves refining the scoping and ownership of these temporary data structures within the `CTransaction` or `CMutableTransaction` validation context to prevent memory-related undefined behavior.

prs.description: btcsignals: delete broken scoped_connection move assignment
prs.author: thomasbuilds
prs.public_summary: This PR removes a faulty internal mechanism for managing signal connections, preventing potential crashes and ensuring the stable operation of Bitcoin Core's event handling system.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes a broken move assignment operator from the `scoped_connection` class within `btcsignals`. The faulty implementation could lead to double-free issues or incorrect resource management when `scoped_connection` objects were moved, resulting in crashes or undefined behavior. Deleting the problematic operator ensures correct RAII behavior and robust signal connection management.

prs.description: test: interface_http follow-ups
prs.author: pinheadmz
prs.public_summary: This PR provides follow-up improvements and fixes for the test suite related to Bitcoin Core's HTTP interface. It ensures robust and reliable operation of the newly refactored networking components, enhancing overall stability.
prs.technical_summary: This PR enhances the functional test suite by adding new test cases and refining existing ones specifically for the HTTP interface. It addresses gaps and potential regressions introduced by the recent `libevent` removal and custom HTTP server implementation. The tests cover various aspects of HTTP request handling, response parsing, error conditions, and header management, ensuring the custom networking stack behaves as expected under diverse scenarios and providing confidence in the new implementation's reliability.

prs.description: p2p: Drop unsolicited CMPCTBLOCK from non-HB peer
prs.author: davidgumberg
prs.public_summary: This Pull Request enhances network efficiency and security by dropping unsolicited `CMPCTBLOCK` messages from peers that are not designated as high-bandwidth (HB). This prevents potential DoS attacks and ensures efficient block propagation.
prs.technical_summary: The P2P message handling logic is updated to check the 'high-bandwidth' status of a peer before processing incoming `CMPCTBLOCK` messages. If a peer has not been explicitly negotiated or identified as an HB peer (e.g., through feature bits or observed bandwidth characteristics), any `CMPCTBLOCK` message it sends is immediately discarded. This policy prevents non-trusted or misbehaving peers from flooding a node with compact block announcements, focusing resources on legitimate, high-speed block propagation channels.

prs.description: Replace libevent with our own HTTP and socket-handling implementation
prs.author: pinheadmz
prs.public_summary: This significant PR replaces the external `libevent` library with Bitcoin Core's own custom implementation for HTTP and socket handling. This reduces external dependencies, improves control over networking components, and contributes to the project's long-term maintainability and security.
prs.technical_summary: This substantial architectural change involves deprecating and removing the `libevent` dependency by introducing an in-house developed HTTP server and general socket event loop. The new implementation provides tailored asynchronous I/O capabilities, custom-built to fit Bitcoin Core's specific networking requirements. This includes managing socket events, handling HTTP requests, and integrating with existing internal primitives, aiming to enhance performance, reduce the attack surface, and simplify the build process by controlling the entire networking stack.

prs.description: doc: update interface, --stdin flag, `signtx` (#31005)
prs.author: cobratbq
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the documentation for the `signtx` RPC, specifically detailing the use of the new `--stdin` flag. This improves user guidance on how to securely and efficiently provide transaction data for signing.
prs.technical_summary: This documentation update focuses on the `signtx` RPC command, explaining how to leverage the recently introduced `--stdin` flag. It details the process for supplying transaction data via standard input, which is particularly useful for handling large transactions or when integrating with scripting. The update ensures that developer documentation reflects the latest interface capabilities, improving clarity and usability for automation and command-line interactions.

prs.description: stabilize translations by reverting old ids by text content
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This change aims to stabilize translations by reverting to an older method of identifying translatable strings based on their text content rather than volatile IDs. This reduces rework for translators and ensures more consistent translations over time.
prs.technical_summary: The PR modifies the string extraction process (typically involving `xgettext` or similar tools) to use the original English text content as the primary identifier for translation units. This contrasts with systems that might assign numeric or generated IDs that can change with code refactoring, leading to 'lost' translations. By relying on text content, existing translations remain linked as long as the source English string doesn't change, minimizing churn for translation teams and improving the long-term maintainability of localized strings.

prs.description: threadpool: add ranged Submit overload
prs.author: andrewtoth
prs.public_summary: This Pull Request introduces a new overload for submitting tasks to the thread pool that specifically handles ranges of items. It allows developers to more easily and efficiently parallelize operations across collections, which can lead to performance improvements for common processing patterns.
prs.technical_summary: A `Submit` overload is added to the existing `threadpool` class, accepting a range (e.g., iterators or a range object) and a callable. This new method internally partitions the range and submits a separate task for each sub-range or item to the thread pool, effectively parallelizing the operation. This simplifies client code by abstracting away the manual partitioning and task submission required for parallelizing loops over collections, enhancing developer productivity and leveraging available CPU cores more efficiently.

prs.description: Fix startup failure with RLIM_INFINITY fd limits
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a critical bug that prevented Bitcoin Core from starting on systems with 'unlimited' file descriptor limits. It improves the software's robustness and compatibility across various operating environments.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, Bitcoin Core's file descriptor management logic misinterpreted `RLIM_INFINITY` as an excessively large numerical limit, causing startup failures. The fix involves explicitly checking for `RLIM_INFINITY` and treating it as a valid 'unlimited' state. This ensures the application correctly parses system resource limits without error, allowing the node to properly allocate resources and initialize network connections.

prs.description: feefrac: drop comparison and operator{<<,>>} for sorted wrappers
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This change refactors the internal `feefrac` component by removing unnecessary comparison and stream operators for specific wrapper types. This simplifies the codebase, improves type safety, and reduces potential for misuse in internal contexts.
prs.technical_summary: This PR performs a refactoring within the `feefrac` module, targeting internal wrapper classes used for sorted collections. It removes explicit `operator<`, `operator==`, and stream `operator<<` / `operator>>` implementations where these operations are either not logically appropriate for the wrapper's role or are handled by the underlying wrapped type. The goal is to enforce clearer separation of concerns, preventing implicit conversions or comparisons, and ensuring that serialization and ordering logic are applied at the correct abstraction layer within the fee estimation and transaction selection process.

prs.description: p2p: Replace per-peer transaction rate-limiting with global rate limits
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This Pull Request replaces the per-peer transaction rate-limiting mechanism with a single, global rate limit for incoming transactions. This enhances the network's resilience against transaction flooding attacks and ensures fairer resource allocation across all connected peers.
prs.technical_summary: Instead of each connected peer having its own independent token bucket for transaction relay, a single global token bucket is introduced. All incoming transactions from any peer must now draw tokens from this shared global pool before being processed. This prevents a single or small group of malicious peers from exhausting individual peer limits while allowing the node operator to set an overall transaction ingest rate limit, simplifying DoS protection logic and providing a more consistent policy across the P2P network.

prs.description: logging: replace -loglevel with -trace, expose trace logging via RPC
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This PR renames the command-line option for setting logging levels to `-trace` and exposes trace logging functionality via RPC. This provides more granular control over debug logging, making it easier for users and developers to diagnose issues in a running Bitcoin Core node.
prs.technical_summary: The `-loglevel` command-line argument is deprecated in favor of `-trace` for enabling detailed logging. Crucially, this PR also introduces RPC methods (likely `setnetworkactive` or a new dedicated `setlogginglevel`) that allow dynamic adjustment of trace logging categories and verbosity at runtime without requiring a node restart. This involves modifying the logging infrastructure to allow configuration flags to be updated programmatically, providing immediate diagnostic feedback for live systems.

prs.description: wallet, descriptor: Revert `StringType::COMPAT` for Miniscript expressions and drop the concept of a Descriptor ID that can be validated
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR simplifies wallet descriptor handling by removing an unused compatibility string type and an unnecessary descriptor identification concept, making descriptor management more robust and easier to maintain.
prs.technical_summary: This PR reverts the use of `StringType::COMPAT` for Miniscript expressions within wallet descriptors, as it proved unnecessary and complicated parsing. Concurrently, it removes the concept of a "Descriptor ID that can be validated," simplifying descriptor identification by relying solely on the descriptor string itself. This change streamlines descriptor parsing, reduces potential inconsistencies, and removes a layer of complexity from wallet descriptor management.

prs.description: wallet: switch default optinrbf from true to false
prs.author: rkrux
prs.public_summary: This PR changes the default setting for new transactions in the wallet, making them non-replaceable by default to enhance transaction finality for users.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the default behavior for new transactions created by the Bitcoin Core wallet, setting the `optinrbf` flag to `false` by default. This change means that new wallet transactions will not automatically signal replaceability. Instead, it requires explicit user action to opt into Replace-by-Fee, thereby promoting transaction finality by default.

prs.description: Policy: Report debug message why inputs are non standard
prs.author: ismaelsadeeq
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances Bitcoin Core's debug logging by providing clearer explanations when a transaction input is considered 'non-standard.' This helps users and developers diagnose issues with transaction creation and policy enforcement.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, non-standard input rejections yielded generic debug messages. This PR augments the transaction validation logic, specifically within functions like `CheckStandardInputs`, to include detailed reasons in the debug log. It adds specific logging statements that articulate which non-standard input rule was violated, such as non-minimal push or non-standard script types, aiding in precise debugging of transaction policy rejections.

prs.description: refactor: Properly return from ThreadSafeQuestion signal + btcsignals follow-ups
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors internal signal handling to ensure robust and correct communication between different parts of Bitcoin Core, improving stability and preventing potential issues in concurrent operations.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses a potential issue where `ThreadSafeQuestion` signals might not return correctly, particularly when handlers disconnect during execution. It refactors the signal emission mechanism within `btcsignals` to ensure proper return values and prevent undefined behavior. This enhances the reliability of event-driven communication in multi-threaded contexts.

prs.description: cmake, translation: Use native Qt TS file as source for translations on Transifex
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR streamlines the translation process by using native Qt TS files directly as the source for translations on Transifex. It simplifies the localization workflow, making it easier for translators to contribute accurate and up-to-date translations for the Bitcoin Core UI.
prs.technical_summary: The change involves modifying the CMake build system to directly generate and consume native Qt TS (Translation Source) files for Transifex integration, instead of relying on an intermediate Gettext PO format. This simplifies the toolchain by eliminating a conversion step, ensuring that the translation platform directly works with the preferred Qt format. This reduces potential for format-related issues and aligns the build process more closely with standard Qt localization practices.

prs.description: prevector: simplify operator==
prs.author: purpleKarrot
prs.public_summary: This PR simplifies the equality comparison operator for the `prevector` container, a crucial data structure used throughout Bitcoin Core. The simplification improves code readability and maintainability for this highly optimized, small-buffer vector type.
prs.technical_summary: The `operator==` implementation for `prevector` is refactored to be more concise and robust. This typically involves harmonizing the comparison logic between the small-buffer (inline) and heap-allocated states, possibly by leveraging a common helper function or standard algorithm like `std::equal`. The simplification reduces branching and potential for subtle bugs, making the core data structure's behavior more predictable and easier to audit, without impacting its performance characteristics.

prs.description: rpc: Run type check on decodepsbt result
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the robustness of the `decodepsbt` RPC by adding type checking to its output, preventing potential errors or crashes. This ensures greater stability and reliability for PSBT-related operations.
prs.technical_summary: The `decodepsbt` RPC decodes Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions. This PR introduces strict type checking on the decoded fields before they are returned. It modifies the RPC result generation logic to validate that each field conforms to its expected data type. If an unexpected type is encountered, an RPC error is raised instead of allowing a malformed value to propagate, preventing client-side issues.

prs.description: rpc, net: remove `startingheight` field of `getpeerinfo` RPC and from node state
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This PR removes an unused and potentially misleading `startingheight` field from the `getpeerinfo` RPC and the internal node state. This simplifies the RPC output and internal data structures, focusing on relevant information.
prs.technical_summary: The `startingheight` field in `getpeerinfo` was intended to track a peer's initial synchronization height but was often inaccurate or unreliable. This PR removes `startingheight` from the `CNode` class and the `getpeerinfo` RPC result. Its removal simplifies the `CNode` object, potentially reduces network message overhead, and streamlines the `getpeerinfo` output by eliminating a data point that provided little value and could cause confusion.

prs.description: BIP 323: reserve version bits 5-28 as extra nonce space
prs.author: darosior
prs.public_summary: This PR reserves specific bits in Bitcoin block headers for future use as additional nonce space, laying groundwork for improved mining flexibility and resilience against nonce exhaustion.
prs.technical_summary: This PR implements a preliminary step for BIP 323, reserving bits 5-28 within the block header's `nVersion` field for use as an "extra nonce" space. This modification creates a standardized area for miners to store additional entropy, mitigating current and future nonce exhaustion issues without changing the block hash function. This change does not alter consensus rules but prepares the codebase for eventual activation.

prs.description: validation: Don't add pruned blocks to `m_blocks_unlinked` on startup
prs.author: marcofleon
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes startup for pruned nodes by preventing the unnecessary processing and storage of already-pruned block data, leading to faster initialization and more efficient resource use.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the block validation logic to avoid adding pruned blocks to the `m_blocks_unlinked` data structure during node startup. Pruned blocks lack full transaction data and can never be re-linked to the chain, so including them in this structure consumes memory and processing time unnecessarily. By skipping them, the startup process for pruned nodes is made more efficient and robust.

prs.description: contrib: replace deprecated --deep codesign flag, fix accidental --verify skip on ci
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the macOS code signing script for Bitcoin Core, replacing a deprecated flag and ensuring critical verification steps run during continuous integration. This improves the security and reliability of official macOS releases.
prs.technical_summary: The deprecated `--deep` flag for `codesign` is replaced with modern, granular signing options in the `contrib` script. Additionally, it corrects a flaw in the CI pipeline that caused the `--verify` step to be skipped under certain conditions. The change guarantees consistent execution of `codesign --verify`, ensuring signed binaries meet Apple's security requirements before release.

prs.description: rpc: allow writing UTXO set to a named pipe
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a new RPC feature, enabling users to export the current UTXO set (unspent transaction outputs) to a named pipe. This allows for more flexible and efficient integration with external tools and scripts for data analysis.
prs.technical_summary: This PR extends the `dumptxoutset` RPC command. It introduces an option to specify a named pipe (FIFO) path instead of a regular file for output. The implementation modifies the `dumptxoutset` handler to open the specified path as a pipe, streaming data continuously. This facilitates real-time or streaming analysis by external processes, eliminating the need to write the entire dataset to disk first.

prs.description: test: Fix feature_dbcrash.py --usecli error
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a problem in a key test designed to simulate database crashes, ensuring that Bitcoin Core's database recovery mechanisms are thoroughly and correctly validated.
prs.technical_summary: This PR resolves an error within `feature_dbcrash.py` when executed with the `--usecli` flag, which was causing test failures during CLI-based crash recovery simulations. The fix addresses an incorrect argument or command usage within the test script. This allows the critical database crash and recovery feature to be reliably tested via the command-line interface.

prs.description: Replace boost signals with minimal compatible implementation
prs.author: theuni
prs.public_summary: This PR replaces the external `Boost.Signals` library with a lightweight, custom-developed signal/slot implementation. This effort reduces external dependencies, streamlines the codebase, and improves build times and overall project independence.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes the dependency on `Boost.Signals2` by integrating a custom, header-only implementation of a signal/slot mechanism directly into the Bitcoin Core codebase. The new internal solution provides the essential event subscription and emission capabilities required by various modules, such as for UI updates or peer connection state changes. By replacing the Boost component, the project reduces its reliance on a large external library, simplifying the build process and providing more granular control over the signaling framework's performance and behavior.

prs.description: validation: do not add the snapshot to candidates set of the background chainstate
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes Bitcoin Core's blockchain management by preventing unnecessary processing of snapshot data in the background. This leads to more efficient resource utilization and potentially faster chain synchronization.
prs.technical_summary: The background chainstate's candidate set previously included snapshots, leading to redundant work. This PR modifies the background chainstate logic to explicitly exclude these snapshots. By not considering the main chainstate's snapshot as a candidate for processing, it reduces redundant validation efforts, improves performance during initial block download or reindex, and avoids potential race conditions between validation threads.

prs.description: p2p: Increase inbound capacity for block-relay only connections
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This PR increases the maximum number of inbound connections specifically for peers dedicated to block relay. This improves the efficiency and reliability of block propagation by allowing nodes to connect to more specialized block-relay peers.
prs.technical_summary: The connection manager's logic is modified to adjust the limits for different types of inbound connections. Specifically, the quota for 'block-relay only' connections is increased beyond the general inbound connection limit. This allows a node to maintain more connections with peers primarily used for fast block dissemination (e.g., those that have `feefilter` enabled), optimizing the network topology for rapid block propagation without impacting the overall resource allocation for full-service peers.

prs.description: validation: refactor: remove ConnectTrace
prs.author: stickies-v
prs.public_summary: This PR cleans up and simplifies the internal blockchain validation code by removing an old tracing mechanism called `ConnectTrace`. This improves the readability and maintainability of critical validation logic.
prs.technical_summary: The `ConnectTrace` mechanism was a deprecated or unused debugging/tracing facility within the blockchain connection and validation logic. This PR identifies and removes all instances and definitions related to `ConnectTrace`, including its class definition, member variables, and function calls. Eliminating this dead code makes the validation codebase leaner, reduces cognitive load for developers, and potentially improves compilation times without impacting runtime behavior.

prs.description: ci: Match `VCPKG_HOST_TRIPLET` to `VCPKG_TARGET_TRIPLET`
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR adjusts the Continuous Integration (CI) configuration to ensure that VCPKG's host and target triplets are correctly aligned. This resolves specific cross-compilation issues and improves the reliability of builds for various platforms in the CI pipeline.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the CI scripts, specifically within jobs that utilize VCPKG for dependency management, to explicitly ensure that `VCPKG_HOST_TRIPLET` matches `VCPKG_TARGET_TRIPLET`. This alignment is critical in cross-compilation environments to guarantee that host tools (e.g., compilers, build utilities) built by VCPKG are compatible with the specified target architecture. The fix prevents build failures caused by mismatched host/target triplets, enhancing the robustness of cross-platform CI builds.

prs.description: test: migrate functional test equality asserts to `assert_equal`
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR standardizes the way equality checks are performed across Bitcoin Core's functional test suite. It migrates various assertion patterns to use a dedicated `assert_equal` helper, improving test consistency, readability, and maintainability.
prs.technical_summary: This PR systematically refactors the Python-based functional test suite by replacing direct `assert x == y` statements with calls to the `assert_equal(x, y)` helper function. This change centralizes the logic for equality checks, potentially allowing for more descriptive failure messages and consistent handling of different data types. It is a code quality improvement that simplifies future test maintenance and onboarding by enforcing a uniform style for assertions across the extensive test base.

prs.description: migrate: Handle HD chains that have identical seeds but different IDs
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR improves wallet migration robustness by correctly handling cases where hierarchical deterministic (HD) wallets might share seeds but have different internal identifiers, preventing data loss or misinterpretation during upgrades.
prs.technical_summary: This PR enhances the wallet migration logic to properly distinguish and manage HD chains that originate from identical seeds but possess distinct wallet IDs, a scenario that could arise from different derivation paths or wallet implementations. By explicitly accounting for this edge case, the migration process can correctly identify and integrate these chains, preventing potential conflicts or data corruption during wallet upgrades.

prs.description: torcontrol: Remove libevent usage
prs.author: fjahr
prs.public_summary: This PR removes the `libevent` library dependency specifically from Bitcoin Core's Tor control functionality. This is part of a broader effort to reduce external dependencies and modernize the networking stack, improving maintainability and control.
prs.technical_summary: This PR targets the `torcontrol` module, refactoring its internal logic to eliminate all direct and indirect usage of the `libevent` library. It involves replacing `libevent`-based event loops, socket I/O, and timer management with custom implementations or existing internal utility functions. This isolated removal contributes to the larger architectural goal of shedding the `libevent` dependency from the entire codebase, simplifying the networking stack and providing more granular control over Tor-related communication.

prs.description: Export embedded ASMap RPC
prs.author: fjahr
prs.public_summary: This PR exports an internal Autonomous System (AS) mapping function as a new RPC command. This enables advanced users and developers to inspect and utilize network topology information for debugging peer selection and network analysis.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces a new RPC method, `getasmapinfo` (or similar), which exposes the internal ASMap data structure and its associated lookup functionality. It allows users to query the Autonomous System number corresponding to an IP address, providing visibility into the node's perception of the network's AS-level topology. This RPC call aids in debugging peer selection algorithms, understanding network decentralization, and analyzing connection distribution across various ASNs.

prs.description: Remove Taproot BIP 9 deployment
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR cleans up the Bitcoin Core codebase by removing the now-completed Taproot soft fork signaling mechanism. It streamlines the code and removes obsolete components, making the codebase easier to maintain.
prs.technical_summary: Taproot activation via BIP 9 deployment `csv` (version bits 2, bit 2) has concluded. This PR removes the specific code paths and data structures related to tracking and evaluating BIP 9 signaling for Taproot. This includes purging the `DeploymentPos::TAPROOT` entry and associated logic, thereby eliminating dead code and reducing the complexity of the validation logic as Taproot is now a permanent consensus rule.

prs.description: net: option to disallow v1 connection on ipv4 and ipv6 peers
prs.author: stratospher

prs.description: indexes: Don't wipe indexes again when continuing a prior reindex
prs.author: TheCharlatan
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the efficiency of reindexing operations, preventing unnecessary data deletion if a reindex was previously interrupted and is being resumed. This saves significant time and resources for users who need to rebuild their Bitcoin Core indexes.

This PR modifies the index management logic to detect if an incomplete reindex is being continued. Instead of clearing the database, it now intelligently attempts to pick up where the previous reindex left off, avoiding redundant data deletion and reprocessing of already scanned blocks. This optimization significantly reduces reindexing time by preserving partial progress and only processing the remaining blocks.

prs.description: validation: Disable CheckForkWarningConditions for background chainstate

prs.description: p2p: Reduce bandwidth during initial headers sync when a block is found
prs.author: sdaftuar
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes the initial headers synchronization process for new Bitcoin Core nodes, leading to a significant reduction in network bandwidth usage. It achieves this by intelligently halting unnecessary header requests when a new block is found.
prs.technical_summary: During initial headers sync, nodes typically request headers in batches from peers. If a new block is received via the P2P network (e.g., through an `inv` and `block` message) that extends the best chain or fills a gap in the headers being synced, many pending `getheaders` requests for that range become redundant. This PR implements logic to proactively cancel or avoid sending these redundant `getheaders` messages, leveraging the receipt of new block data to update the required header range. This effectively minimizes superfluous network traffic and accelerates the initial synchronization phase.

prs.description: I2P: add support for transient addresses for outbound connections
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances Bitcoin Core's I2P networking capabilities by adding support for transient addresses for outbound connections. This improves the privacy and anonymity of connections made over the I2P network by making them harder to link.
prs.technical_summary: This change modifies the I2P network integration within Bitcoin Core to utilize transient I2P destinations for outbound connection attempts. Instead of reusing a static destination, a new, short-lived I2P address is generated for each outbound connection. This makes it more difficult for observers to correlate multiple connections from the same node, enhancing connection-level privacy within the I2P network.

This significantly improves the robustness of the wallet system, preventing data loss and enhancing user experience even with corrupted wallet files.

This fix involves adding more robust error handling and validation around descriptor parsing during wallet loading. Instead of crashing, the wallet will now gracefully handle invalid descriptors, perhaps logging a warning and skipping the problematic descriptor, allowing the rest of the wallet to load and preserving data integrity.

This change updates the RPC output schema to mark the `address` field as optional. By doing so, the API better reflects the underlying transaction data structures, allowing RPC clients to handle cases where a single, unambiguous address is not present without encountering parsing errors or making incorrect assumptions, thus improving API robustness.

The fix involves adapting the test logic, such as modifying address generation expectations or transaction parsing, to correctly account for the distinct behaviors and limitations of these legacy wallet types. This ensures consistent test passing for both descriptor and BDB-only wallet configurations.

prs.description: p2p: ProcessHeadersMessage(): fix received_new_header
prs.author: LarryRuane
prs.public_summary: This PR corrects an internal flag (`received_new_header`) within the peer-to-peer (P2P) module, ensuring it accurately tracks when new headers are received. This improves the node's ability to efficiently process and sync with the blockchain.
prs.technical_summary: This PR corrects a logical error in the `ProcessHeadersMessage()` function within the P2P layer where the `received_new_header` boolean flag was being incorrectly set or reset. Specifically, the flag was only being set to `true` if a header was *connected* to the chain, not just *received*. The fix ensures `received_new_header` is set to `true` whenever a valid, previously unknown header is received, even if it's not immediately connected to the active chain, thereby improving the accuracy of tracking header reception for peer management and sync logic.

This PR adjusts the Guix build recipe to explicitly set `--build={arch}-guix-linux-gnu` for the cross-compilation toolchain. This ensures that the build system correctly identifies the native host architecture for bootstrapping and avoids conflicts with the target architecture, thereby stabilizing the Guix cross-compilation process across different platforms.

prs.description: wallet: Fix nNextResend data race in ResubmitWalletTransactions
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves a data race in the wallet's transaction resubmission logic, preventing potential issues with transactions not being re-broadcast correctly. It significantly improves the reliability of transaction propagation for wallet users.
prs.technical_summary: A data race was identified involving the `nNextResend` member variable within the `ResubmitWalletTransactions` function. This variable, which tracks the next time a transaction should be re-broadcast, was not adequately protected by a lock, leading to potential concurrent modifications and incorrect state. This PR introduces proper locking mechanisms, likely using `cs_wallet`, around accesses to `nNextResend` to ensure atomic updates and maintain data integrity. This is the original fix, later backported to 24.x.

prs.technical_summary: With Segwit having been active for many years, the code paths and RPC fields introduced solely for compatibility with pre-Segwit mining software are no longer necessary. This PR identifies and excises these legacy components, which might include specific flags in `getblocktemplate` responses, internal logic to handle non-Segwit transaction formats, or conditional code branches based on Segwit activation status. The removal directly reduces the overall code footprint, improving readability, maintainability, and potentially slightly enhancing performance by eliminating dead code paths from the mining and RPC subsystems.

prs.description: wallet: Fix sendall with watchonly wallets and specified inputs
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug in the wallet where using the 'sendall' function with watch-only wallets and specified inputs would fail. This improves the reliability of transaction creation for users managing funds in advanced watch-only setups.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, the `sendall` RPC method incorrectly attempted to sign inputs in watch-only wallets when `selected_inputs` was used, leading to an error. The fix modifies the input selection and transaction creation logic to correctly identify and use only spendable inputs when `sendall` is called on a watch-only wallet with specific inputs, ensuring that no signing is attempted on non-spendable outputs. This adjustment prevents premature failure and allows for correct transaction construction by either consuming only spendable funds or providing a more accurate error if spendable inputs are insufficient.

prs.description: [24.x] init: abort if i2p/cjdns are chosen via -onlynet but are unreachable
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR ensures Bitcoin Core aborts startup if configured to exclusively use unreachable networks like I2P or CJDNS. This prevents nodes from operating in an unintended isolated state.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, if a user specified `-onlynet=i2p` or `-onlynet=cjdns` but the respective proxy or network interface was unavailable, Bitcoin Core would still initialize, leading to a silently disconnected node. This PR introduces a check during early initialization to verify the reachability of these exclusive networks. If they are unreachable, the node now explicitly aborts, ensuring the node doesn't run in a non-functional state. This is a backport to the 24.x release branch.

prs.description: wallet: allow psbtbumpfee to work with txs with external inputs
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the `psbtbumpfee` RPC, allowing it to increase fees for partially signed Bitcoin transactions (PSBTs) even when they contain inputs not directly managed by the wallet. This improves the flexibility and usability of fee bumping for a broader range of transactions.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, `psbtbumpfee` required all inputs in a PSBT to be recognized by the wallet for successful fee bumping. This change extends its functionality by ensuring that external inputs—those not owned by the local wallet—are correctly preserved and handled during the transaction replacement process. The underlying logic is modified to ensure the fee-bumped transaction correctly references and includes these external inputs without requiring wallet ownership, thereby enabling bumping for transactions with mixed input sources.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 22.0.

prs.description: wallet: Reorder locks in dumpwallet to avoid lock order assertion
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR reorders internal locks within the `dumpwallet` function to prevent potential deadlocks or assertion failures. This improves the stability and reliability of the wallet export functionality.
prs.technical_summary: The `dumpwallet` function previously acquired multiple mutexes or locks in an order that could lead to contention issues or deadlock conditions. This change carefully resequences the acquisition of these locks, ensuring a consistent and safe locking hierarchy. By adhering to a strict lock ordering, the PR eliminates race conditions and guarantees the correct execution of wallet dumping operations.

prs.description: build: Perform boost::process detection with BOOST_CPPFLAGS
prs.author: laanwj
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the Bitcoin Core build system's ability to detect `boost::process` correctly across various environments. This ensures more reliable compilation and broader compatibility for the software.
prs.technical_summary: The PR addresses an issue in the build system where `boost::process` detection was unreliable by correctly utilizing `BOOST_CPPFLAGS`. This ensures that necessary preprocessor definitions and include paths are consistently applied during the configure stage, resolving compilation errors that previously occurred due to incorrect Boost library linkage or header discovery.

prs.description: clientversion: No suffix #if CLIENT_VERSION_IS_RELEASE
prs.author: dongcarl
prs.public_summary: This PR modifies how the client version string is generated, ensuring that official release builds do not include development suffixes. This helps in clearly distinguishing stable releases from development snapshots.
prs.technical_summary: This change involves adjusting the preprocessor directives in `src/clientversion.h` or related files. Specifically, it likely wraps the inclusion of version suffixes (e.g., `-rcX`, `-dev`, `(build XX)`) within an `#if !CLIENT_VERSION_IS_RELEASE` block. This ensures that when `CLIENT_VERSION_IS_RELEASE` is defined (for official releases), these suffixes are omitted, resulting in a cleaner and more consistent version string like "0.21.2" instead of "0.21.2-rc1" as reported by the `getnetworkinfo` RPC and GUI.

prs.description: Randomize message processing peer order
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR improves network resilience and privacy by randomizing the order in which messages from connected peers are processed. This helps to mitigate certain types of network attacks and makes it harder for adversaries to infer network topology.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the P2P networking layer's message handling logic. It introduces randomization when selecting which peer's messages to process next, instead of a fixed order. This likely involves shuffling the list of active peers or employing a random selection mechanism before iterating through their message queues, thereby obscuring message propagation patterns.

prs.description: net, rpc: expose high bandwidth mode state via getpeerinfo
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This feature exposes a peer's 'high bandwidth mode' state through the `getpeerinfo` RPC, providing users and network analysts with more insight into peer capabilities and network behavior. It enhances network diagnostic tools.
prs.technical_summary: The PR extends the JSON output of the `getpeerinfo` RPC call to include a new field indicating whether a connected peer is operating in 'high bandwidth mode'. This mode is typically determined by peer service flags or observed network behavior, like active compact block relay. The networking layer's `CNode` or `CNodeState` objects are updated to track this state, and the RPC handler is modified to query and present this information to the user.

prs.description: wallet: Add missing BlockUntilSyncedToCurrentChain
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances wallet reliability by ensuring that certain operations wait until the wallet is fully synchronized with the current blockchain state. This prevents transactions from being built or broadcast based on outdated information, improving the accuracy of balances and transaction validity.
prs.technical_summary: The change introduces `BlockUntilSyncedToCurrentChain` calls to critical wallet code paths, ensuring that operations like coin selection, transaction creation, or balance queries execute only after the wallet's internal chain tip matches the node's current best chain. This prevents race conditions and stale data issues by blocking execution until the `CWallet`'s internal state reflects the current `ChainActive()` tip. It guarantees a consistent view of the UTXO set and transaction history before proceeding with sensitive wallet operations.

prs.description: [22.x] rc2 backports
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR bundles several backports to the `22.x` release candidate 2 branch. These changes integrate critical fixes and minor improvements, ensuring the stability and readiness of the upcoming 22.x release.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request constitutes a set of cherry-picked commits from the `master` branch, specifically targeting the `22.x` release candidate 2 (rc2) branch. It typically involves applying a curated list of non-controversial bug fixes, performance enhancements, or minor feature updates deemed essential for the stability and quality of the release candidate. Each backported commit is reviewed for compatibility with the `22.x` codebase, and any necessary merge conflicts are resolved to ensure a clean integration without regressions for the pending release.

prs.description: addrman: reset I2P ports in all "new" buckets
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the network address manager's handling of I2P addresses by ensuring that I2P-specific ports are correctly reset. This helps maintain the health and connectivity of the P2P network, especially for I2P nodes.
prs.technical_summary: The `addrman` component needs to properly manage I2P peer addresses, which use distinct port allocation strategies. This PR addresses an issue where I2P ports might not be correctly initialized or reset when an I2P address is moved into a 'new' bucket. The fix modifies the `CAddrInfo` update logic to explicitly reset the I2P port field to zero when a new I2P address entry is created or moved, ensuring proper re-evaluation on subsequent connection attempts.

prs.description: contrib: add torv3 seed nodes for testnet, drop v2 ones
prs.author: laanwj
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the testnet seed nodes to exclusively use Tor v3 addresses, removing the deprecated Tor v2 addresses. It improves the privacy and security of testnet connections for users relying on Tor.
prs.technical_summary: This contribution updates the hardcoded seed nodes specifically for the Bitcoin testnet within the `contrib` directory. It involves adding new Tor v3 onion service addresses, which are longer and provide enhanced cryptography, to the list. Simultaneously, it removes all entries for the older, less secure Tor v2 onion services. This change ensures that testnet nodes connecting via Tor use the latest protocol version, aligning with the broader Tor network's deprecation of v2 services and improving the robustness of peer discovery over Tor.

prs.description: [0.21] Backport: Reset scantxoutset progress before inferring descriptors
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR, a backport for version 0.21, ensures accurate wallet descriptor inference by resetting the scantxoutset progress. This prevents potential issues where previous scan states could lead to incorrect or incomplete descriptor generation.
prs.technical_summary: Wallet descriptors are used to describe sets of UTXOs for a wallet, and `scantxoutset` is a process to find these. Before inferring descriptors, it's crucial to have a clean state to ensure reliability. This PR ensures that any in-progress or residual state from a prior `scantxoutset` operation is cleared, guaranteeing that descriptor inference starts with a fresh scan and produces correct results for wallet management.

prs.description: [0.21] gitian: Use custom MacOS code signing tool
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This update improves the reproducible build process for Bitcoin Core on macOS by implementing a custom code signing tool. This ensures the integrity and authenticity of Bitcoin Core executables distributed for Apple systems.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request integrates a custom macOS code signing utility into the Gitian build process for the 0.21 release branch. Traditionally, macOS code signing can introduce non-determinism due to reliance on specific system tools or certificates. The custom tool aims to provide a more controlled and reproducible signing step, ensuring that the resulting macOS binaries are properly signed while maintaining Gitian's core principle of bit-for-bit identical builds, thus enhancing the security and verifiable authenticity of the macOS distribution.

prs.description: [0.21] qt: Pre-0.21.2rc2 translations update
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the translations for the Bitcoin Core graphical user interface (GUI) ahead of the 0.21.2 release candidate. It ensures that the software is more accessible and user-friendly for non-English speakers.
prs.technical_summary: This involves pulling in updated `.ts` (translation source) files, typically generated from Transifex or a similar localization platform, and recompiling the `.qm` (Qt message) files. These updates reflect string changes, new features, or corrections made since the last translation snapshot for the Qt GUI, ensuring the latest localized text is available for the upcoming release. The `lupdate` and `lrelease` tools are used in the build process.

This architectural refactoring enables a more decoupled approach to signature validation, potentially allowing for batch processing of cryptographic checks or improved resource management during transaction evaluation, thereby enhancing throughput and extensibility.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.21.0.

prs.description: [backport] build: Avoid secp256k1.h include from system
prs.author: dergoegge
prs.public_summary: This backport PR improves the build system by preventing Bitcoin Core from accidentally including a system-wide `secp256k1.h` header. This ensures that the correct, bundled version of the cryptographic library is always used, avoiding potential build issues or runtime inconsistencies.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the `depends` build system or the main project's CMake/autotools configuration to explicitly prioritize the vendored `secp256k1` library header (`secp256k1.h`) over any system-installed versions. This is typically achieved by adjusting include paths or compiler flags to ensure `-I/path/to/local/secp256k1` takes precedence. The change prevents potential ABI mismatches or build failures that could arise from using an incompatible `secp256k1` header.

prs.description: test: Fix intermittent issue in mempool_compatibility
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves an intermittent test failure related to the mempool's compatibility with various transaction types. This improves the reliability of our automated tests, ensuring the mempool behaves as expected under all conditions.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses an intermittent failure observed in the `mempool_compatibility` test suite. The issue likely stemmed from timing-sensitive interactions or specific transaction relay sequences that, under certain test execution conditions, led to non-deterministic outcomes. The fix identifies and rectifies the root cause, possibly through improved synchronization mechanisms, stricter transaction ordering within tests, or adjusted timeouts, thereby enhancing the determinism and stability of mempool-related integration tests without altering core mempool logic.

prs.description: P2P: Mempool tracks locally submitted transactions to improve wallet privacy
prs.author: amitiuttarwar
prs.public_summary: This PR significantly improves wallet privacy by enabling the node's mempool to track transactions submitted by the local wallet separately from those received from peers. This prevents locally generated transactions from being easily linked to the originating node through standard mempool queries.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation introduces a new attribute or flag within the mempool's transaction data structure to mark transactions that originate from the local node via RPCs like `sendrawtransaction`. When RPC calls such as `getmempoolentry` or `getrawmempool` are executed, they now filter out these 'local' transactions by default, unless explicitly requested. This creates a logical partition in mempool visibility, making it harder for network observers to correlate specific transactions with the user's node, thereby bolstering privacy without affecting global transaction propagation.

prs.description: qt: Pre-splitoff translations update
prs.author: laanwj
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the graphical user interface (GUI) translations for Bitcoin Core, preparing for a future modularization of the translation process. It improves the user experience for non-English speakers by ensuring the application text is up-to-date and accurate.
prs.technical_summary: This PR incorporates the latest translations for the Qt GUI, specifically in preparation for a 'splitoff' of the translation infrastructure. It likely involves merging updated `.ts` (Qt Linguist translation source) files, which will be compiled into `.qm` (Qt message) files. The 'pre-splitoff' suggests a refactoring effort is underway to make the translation system more independent or easier to manage, making this an intermediary update before that larger architectural change.

prs.description: wallet: fix potential division by 0 in WalletLogPrintf
prs.author: jonasschnelli
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves a potential bug in the wallet's logging function that could lead to a crash if certain values were zero. It improves the robustness of the wallet by preventing division-by-zero errors in its internal diagnostics.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces a check to prevent a division-by-zero error in the `WalletLogPrintf` function, specifically when calculating rates or percentages. It likely involves adding a conditional guard (e.g., `if (denominator != 0)`) before performing a division operation. This ensures the logger gracefully handles edge cases where a divisor might unexpectedly be zero, preventing application crashes and improving the stability of wallet-related diagnostic output.

prs.description: doc: Move 0.21.0 release notes from wiki
prs.author: laanwj
prs.public_summary: This PR migrates the official release notes for Bitcoin Core version 0.21.0 from an external wiki to the project's repository. This ensures that release information is more accessible and consistently versioned alongside the code.
prs.technical_summary: This change involves transferring the content of the 0.21.0 release notes from an external MediaWiki instance into a dedicated documentation file within the Bitcoin Core repository. The existing documentation structure will be updated to reference this new internal file. This centralizes release information and improves maintainability by integrating it into the standard Git workflow, enhancing discoverability and reducing reliance on external documentation platforms.

prs.description: build: Drop make dist in gitian builds
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR streamlines the Gitian build process by removing an unnecessary `make dist` step. This optimizes build times and reduces complexity for creating reproducible Bitcoin Core binaries.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes the `make dist` target execution from the Gitian build scripts. The `make dist` command is typically used to create a source tarball for distribution, but in the context of Gitian builds, the source is already directly pulled from Git. Eliminating this redundant step reduces disk I/O, saves CPU cycles, and simplifies the build manifest, leading to faster and more efficient reproducible builds without altering the final binary artifacts.

prs.description: build: replace libdmg and genisoimage with xorriso
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR streamlines the build process for macOS release artifacts by replacing `libdmg` and `genisoimage` with `xorriso`. This improves maintainability and simplifies the dependency stack for creating disk images.
prs.technical_summary: The build system's reliance on external utilities `libdmg` and `genisoimage` for creating macOS `.dmg` and generic `.iso` release packages is replaced by the more modern `xorriso` tool. This refactoring standardizes the creation of ISO 9660 filesystems and DMGs, which simplifies build scripts, reduces the number of external dependencies, and enhances cross-platform build consistency.

prs.description: rpc: deprecate banscore field in getpeerinfo
prs.author: jonatack
prs.public_summary: This PR deprecates the 'banscore' field in the `getpeerinfo` RPC command. This change helps streamline the RPC interface by removing a less-used or potentially misleading field, preparing for future API improvements and reducing client-side complexity.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation involves marking the `banscore` field as deprecated within the `getpeerinfo` RPC method definition. While the field might still be present for a transition period, callers are advised to no longer rely on it. This signals a future removal, guiding RPC client developers to adapt their integrations.

prs.description: Bugfix: RPC/Wallet: Make BTC/kB and sat/B fee modes work sanely
prs.author: luke-jr
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug in the RPC and Wallet components to ensure that fee rates specified in 'BTC/kB' and 'sat/B' are calculated and applied correctly. This makes transaction fee estimation more reliable and predictable for users and applications using these units.
prs.technical_summary: This PR targets the `RPC` and `Wallet` subsystems, specifically correcting the logic for parsing and applying transaction fee rates. The fix addresses erroneous calculations or conversions when fees are provided in `BTC/kB` or `sat/B` units, ensuring the wallet accurately interprets these values and derives the correct fee amount for transactions, likely involving adjustments to unit conversion factors.

prs.description: build: add stack-clash and control-flow protection options to hardening flags
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This build system improvement adds modern compiler hardening flags to protect Bitcoin Core executables against sophisticated memory-corruption attacks like stack-clash and control-flow exploits. It significantly enhances the security posture of running nodes.
prs.technical_summary: The PR modifies the build configuration (e.g., `configure.ac` and `Makefile.am`) to enable specific compiler flags such as `-fstack-protector-strong` and control-flow integrity (CFI) options (e.g., `-fcf-protection=full`). These flags instruct the compiler to insert runtime checks and generate more secure code, making it substantially harder for attackers to exploit buffer overflows or hijack program execution flow, thereby mitigating common classes of software vulnerabilities.

prs.description: wallet: fix change detection of imported internal descriptors
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug where the wallet failed to correctly detect change outputs for addresses derived from imported internal descriptors. This ensures that funds sent as change to these addresses are properly recognized and accounted for in the wallet balance.
prs.technical_summary: When importing a descriptor wallet that uses internal descriptors for change addresses, the existing wallet logic had an oversight in matching change outputs back to these specific descriptor types. This PR targets the `IsChange()` method within `CWallet`'s transaction scanning. It ensures that the derivation path and script type associated with an output correctly map to the imported internal descriptor for change, thereby accurately identifying and confirming internal change addresses.

prs.description: [wip] build: Switch from C++11 to C++17
prs.author: practicalswift
prs.public_summary: This work-in-progress Pull Request initiates the upgrade of Bitcoin Core's codebase from the C++11 standard to C++17. This modernizes the build environment, allowing developers to leverage new language features for improved performance, safety, and maintainability.
prs.technical_summary: Migrating a large codebase from C++11 to C++17 involves updating compiler flags, build system configurations (e.g., `configure.ac`, `Makefile.am`), and potentially refactoring code. This PR would involve initial changes to `AM_CXXFLAGS` or `CXXSTD` variables, enabling C++17 features, and addressing any immediate compilation errors or warnings. The benefits include access to `std::optional`, `std::variant`, `std::filesystem`, and other C++17 features that can simplify code and improve type safety.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.20.1.

prs.description: Fix locking on WSL using flock instead of fcntl
prs.author: meshcollider
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves an issue with file locking on Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) by switching from `fcntl` to `flock` for file locking. This ensures correct and reliable operation of Bitcoin Core when run in WSL environments.
prs.technical_summary: File locking is critical for preventing data corruption from multiple Bitcoin Core instances. On Linux, `fcntl` and `flock` are used for file locking, but they behave differently, especially in environments like WSL. This PR identified that `fcntl` locks behave unreliably in WSL, likely due to how WSL's kernel compatibility layer translates system calls. Switching to `flock` provides a more robust and consistently behaving locking mechanism under WSL, ensuring mutual exclusion for critical files such as `debug.log` or the wallet lock file.

prs.description: qt: Add missing QPainterPath include
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a build issue in the Qt user interface by adding a necessary header file, ensuring the graphical interface compiles correctly. This resolves a compilation error and improves the reliability of the build process for GUI components.
prs.technical_summary: This PR is a build system or code fix specific to the `qt` (graphical user interface) component. It addresses a compilation error by adding `#include <QPainterPath>` to one or more source files where the `QPainterPath` class was used but its header was not explicitly included, resolving an 'undefined symbol' error during the build.

prs.description: [0.20] Fix GBT: Restore "!segwit" and "csv" to "rules" key
prs.author: luke-jr
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug in the GetBlockTemplate (GBT) RPC by restoring the "rules" key to correctly include `!segwit` and `csv` (CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY) when applicable. This ensures mining pools using GBT receive accurate information about consensus rules, preventing block rejections due to outdated templates.
prs.technical_summary: GetBlockTemplate (GBT) is an RPC method used by miners to construct new blocks. The `rules` field in the GBT response indicates the consensus rules active on the network. This bug meant that `!segwit` and `csv` were erroneously omitted. The fix involves correcting the logic within the `getblocktemplate` RPC implementation to always include these rules in the `rules` array when they are relevant for block validity, ensuring miners receive a complete and correct set of rules for constructing valid blocks.
